belief: My faith is only as strong as my feelings.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that your faith is only as strong as your feelings, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Church experiences that focused on emotional highs. Feeling spiritually strong only after retreats, worship nights, or revivals. Depression or exhaustion that made faith feel weak. Hearing that a real Christian always feels on fire for God. Comparing your feelings with others’ expressions of faith.
teaches: Faith is trust in God and His Word, not a feeling. We walk by faith, not by sight. Faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see. It comes by hearing the word of Christ. In Lamentations, the writer felt crushed, yet he called to mind God’s faithfulness and found hope. Feelings rise and fall; God’s faithfulness does not.
self_statements: I don’t feel anything, so my faith must be weak.
I’m only close to God when I feel it.
My faith comes and goes with my mood.
If I don’t feel excited, I must be backsliding.
errors: Measuring faith by how you feel.
Believing faith is either fully felt or absent.
Turning one dry day into “my faith is gone.”
Measuring your faith by others’ emotions.
questions: What does it mean to walk by faith, not by sight?
Is faith a feeling or trust in God’s promises?
What did the writer of Lamentations do when he felt crushed?
Where does faith come from, according to Romans 10:17?
Have my feelings ever been low while my trust remained?
Is God’s faithfulness affected by my mood?
What could I do to strengthen faith on a day I feel nothing?
truth: My faith is not only as strong as my feelings. Faith is trust in God and His Word. I walk by faith, not by sight or feeling. My emotions rise and fall, but God’s faithfulness is great and His mercies are new every morning. I can strengthen my faith by hearing His Word.
hw_questions: What does it mean to walk by faith?
Is faith a feeling or trust?
What did Lamentations’ writer call to mind?
Have I trusted God when I felt low?
Is God’s faithfulness affected by my mood?
hw_truths: I walk by faith, not by feelings.
Faith is trust in God and His Word.
My feelings rise and fall; God’s faithfulness does not.
Faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
I can call to mind God’s faithfulness and have hope.
I can rejoice in God even when I feel little.
log: Each day, write one action I took in faith, whether or not I felt anything.
name_example: Yet Sarah calls this to mind, and therefore she has hope: Because of the loving devotion of the LORD she is not consumed, for His mercies never fail.
actions: Read Scripture for ten minutes each day this week,
whether or not you feel like it.
Write a list of God’s past faithfulness
in your life and read it on low days.
Do one act of obedience this week
that you don’t feel like doing, and notice what happens.
and note how many faithful people acted without seeing the results.
prayer: Father, thank You that my faith rests on You and Your Word, not on my feelings. Help me reject the lie that my faith is only as strong as my feelings. Teach me to walk by faith, to call to mind Your faithfulness, and to keep trusting You on dry days. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
